'''''Ceiba aesculifolia''''' is a tree belonging to the [[Malvaceae]] [[Family (taxonomy)|family]]. It can reach up to {{convert|30|m|ft|abbr=on}} in height and has a thick trunk. In its [[Juvenile (organism)|juvenile]] stages, the trunk is covered with large, conical thorns. The fruit is a giant capsule that encloses its seeds in a thick layer of soft, white, silky fiber. This fiber has been used to stuff mattresses. Handicrafts are made from the bark and thorns. The tree has medicinal properties. It is the sacred tree of the [[Maya peoples|Mayans]].

It is also known as ''ceiba'' and ''pochote''.<ref name="inaturalist-Ceiba aesculifolia">{{inaturalist taxon|209891|Ceiba aesculifolia}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Ceiba aesculifolia'' reaches a height of {{convert|30|m|ft|abbr=on}}, with a trunk densely covered with thorns. It has 5–7 foliolate leaves. Leaflets of range in shape from [[obovate]] to oblong-[[elliptic]] and are between 3–10 cm long and 1–4 cm wide. They can be [[acuminate]], [[Cuneate leaf|cuneate]], serrated at least towards the apex, glabrous or densely pubescent. Solitary flowers appear in the axils of fallen leaves or somewhat grouped towards the apices of the branches, whitish turning brown inside; irregular and slightly lobed calyx, {{convert|1.5|-|3|cm|in|abbr=on}} long. Petals are {{convert|8|-|16|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, with dense yellowish-brown pubescence on the outside; filaments form a narrow, pubescent column approximately {{convert|1.5|-|2|cm|in|abbr=on}} long. Fruits produced by the plant range from {{convert|12|-|15|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and can be up to {{convert|8|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide.<ref name="Trop"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''C. aesculifolia'' is found in low, dry, [[deciduous forests]], as well as north-central and Pacific zones, at altitudes ranging from {{convert|20|-|850|m|ft|abbr=on}}. It lives from [[Mexico]] to [[Costa Rica]]. It flowers January to April, and fruits May to June.

== Taxonomy ==
The species was initially described as ''Bombax aesculifolium'' by [[Carl Sigismund Kunth]] in 1821,<ref>{{Cite taxon |Tropicos |access-date=2023-05-15 |title=''Bombax aesculifolium'' Kunth |id=3900011 }}</ref> and was later transferred to the genus ''[[Ceiba]]'' by [[James Britten]] and [[Edmund Gilbert Baker]] in 1896.<ref name="Trop">{{Cite taxon |Tropicos |access-date=6 June 2013 |title=''Ceiba aesculifolia'' (Kunth) Britten & Baker f. |id=3900202 }}</ref>
